title: Islam: begin with mercy
hookLine: almost every chapter opens: in the name of God, most gracious, most merciful (Quran 1:1)

cards: Per my last message. We need to talk. A Monday, begun with a groan.

First words set the weather for everything after them. Open a Qur'an to almost any chapter, one hundred thirteen of its one hundred fourteen, and before law or story or warning, the same opening line is waiting.
It names God, and then, twice over, it names mercy. Today: Rahman, and the habit of beginning with mercy.

teach.b: The line is called the basmala, and it opens the very first chapter. In Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful."
In Arabic: bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Two names for God, both grown from the same three-letter root, r-h-m.
One common reading: Rahman is the vast, overflowing mercy that covers everything and everyone; Rahim is the steady, caring mercy that stays close.
The same root gives the Arabic word rahim, the womb. A hadith reports God saying: I am ar-Rahman; I created the womb and gave it a name drawn from my own.
The language ties mercy to a mother's love for the child she carries.

teach.h: MY MERCY PREVAILS OVER MY WRATH.
teach.b: Another hadith, in Sahih al-Bukhari, says that when God created the world, God wrote: my mercy prevails over my wrath.
And another, that God divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent just one down to earth; from that single part, a mother animal lifts her hoof so as not to hurt her young.

Only the ninth chapter doesn't open with the basmala, and scholars give different reasons. But the line appears inside chapter twenty-seven, in a letter from Solomon, so the count still comes to one hundred fourteen.
Muslims say bismillah before eating, driving, starting work, even entering a room.
To begin with God's name is to begin with mercy, before the day's weather is set.

how: Muslims recite the basmala at the start of each chapter of the Qur'an and say bismillah before eating, traveling, working and many ordinary acts.

games.q: a hadith says God divided mercy into a hundred parts. how many were sent down to earth?
games.why: just one part, the hadith says; from it, even a mother animal lifts her hoof so as not to hurt her young.

practice: Think of the next thing you'll start, a message, a meeting, a chore, a conversation with someone difficult, and picture its first words.
Now soften them: per my last message becomes thanks for this; we need to talk becomes I've been thinking about you. If you pray, you might begin with bismillah.

wordCard.voice: Rahman. The Most Merciful: mercy that overflows, from the same root as the word for womb, named at the start of almost every chapter. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Merciful, from the root r-h-m.

carryVoice: Your line: begin with mercy. Two names, one root, and both of them mercy. See you tomorrow.
